headline: Sensex slumps over 1,000 points amid global sell-off with metals and banking stocks leading the downturn

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Global market sell-off weighing heavily on domestic investor sentiment.
Sharp decline and selling pressure in metal and banking sectors.
Market bulls taking a breather after recent sessions of gains.
Intraday profit booking pulling the Sensex down by over 1,100 points.
whatHappening: Sensex plummeted over 1,000 points while Nifty dropped below the 25,500 level.
Tata Steel crashed nearly 9%, leading the slump in metal stocks.
Dalmia Bharat approved a share buyback plan worth ₹700 crore via the open market route.
Supreme Court rejected the Income Tax Department's bid to reopen a decades-old Reliance merger tax case.
summary:
Indian equity markets experienced a sharp sell-off today, with the Sensex tumbling over 1,000 points driven down by global cues and sector-wide losses in metals and banks.
Tata Steel led the decliners after crashing nearly 9%, whereas Dalmia Bharat approved a ₹700 crore buyback.
In legal developments, the Supreme Court refused to reopen a decades-old Reliance merger tax case.
